options.tradeoff: Evaluate each event against the state reduced up to just before it, as the CLI already does at write time. Re-attachment ends the old session's ownership from that point on, including the drafting session's. Costs an incremental reduce in check.
Keep each task's attached sessions with time ranges and check against them. Same result, more bookkeeping.

data.question: Lane checks for past events use the final state (GitHub #14), so re-attaching a task to a new session makes the old session's legitimate handoffs look like lane violations. Since the control loop now raises a tier-2 decision for every conflict, this would flood the lead with false alarms. Which rule applies?
data.title: Check each event's lane against the state when it was written
